24 A motor boat vibrates in the water so that it produces water waves of frequency 0.20 Hz. The
speed of these waves in the water is 20 m s–1. The motor boat moves with a speed of 5.0 m s–1
directly towards a stationary sailing boat.
The Doppler effect equation for sound waves also applies to water waves.
What is the frequency with which the waves hit the stationary sailing boat?
A
0.15 Hz
B
0.16 Hz
C
0.25 Hz
D
0.27 Hz

hints: Notice the source speed $5.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards the stationary observer compared with wave speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ - the source is catching up with the $0.20\text{ Hz}$ waves it emits.
For a moving source the observed wavelength is shortened to $\lambda_o = (v-v_s)/f_s$ because each new crest is emitted closer to the last one.
Calculate $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f_s v/(v-v_s)$ with $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s = 5.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and check whether the result must be larger than $0.20\text{ Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify the situation: wave speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, source frequency $f_s = 0.20\text{ Hz}$, source speed $v_s = 5.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards a stationary observer.
Recall the Doppler rule for a source moving towards a stationary observer: observed wavelength is reduced because the source follows its emitted crest, so $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$.

First find the emitted wavelength: $\lambda = v/f_s = 20/0.20 = 100\text{ m}$. In one period $T = 1/0.20 = 5.0\text{ s}$ the source moves $v_s T = 25\text{ m}$ forward, so $\lambda_o = 100 - 25 = 75\text{ m}$.
Use $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ for the stationary sailing boat: $f_o = 20/75 = 0.266...\text{ Hz}$.
Equivalently, $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s) = 0.20 \times 20/(20-5.0) = 4.0/15 \approx 0.27\text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$, which is higher than $0.20\text{ Hz}$ as expected for approach.

A.explanation: Too low for an approaching source. Frequency must increase above $0.20\text{ Hz}$, not decrease to $0.15\text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: This is $0.20 \times 20/(20+5) = 0.16\text{ Hz}$, the frequency if the motor boat moved away from the sailing boat.

C.explanation: This is $0.20 \times (20+5)/20 = 0.25\text{ Hz}$, which applies to a moving observer, not to a moving source catching up with its own waves.

D.explanation: Approaching source shortens the wavelength, so $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s) = 0.27\text{ Hz}$.
